title: Adding a Passenger Pickup Stop: Confirm the Whole Ride
description: Adding someone at another hotel or office? Confirm the extra pickup, combined passengers and luggage, revised route, timing and quote before the ride.
cta: Plan every passenger pickup in one complete request.
image_alt: A traveler with a rolling suitcase waits outside a modern building as a colleague approaches along the sidewalk.
body:
To add a passenger pickup to an arranged ride, ask the transportation provider to confirm the revised itinerary before the extra traveler relies on it. Give the new pickup address, who is joining, their luggage, the proposed stop order and any arrival deadline. Obtain acknowledgment of the route, timing, vehicle suitability and any revised quote or terms.

An extra passenger and an extra pickup are different changes. Someone joining at the original meeting point changes the party details; someone waiting at another hotel or office also changes the journey. Include both when they apply.

Describe who joins where

Start with a stop-by-stop passenger list. Record how many people and bags are aboard after each pickup, rather than giving only the starting count. If a colleague has a large case or someone needs a child seat, tell the provider before confirming the change. Our luggage-planning guide explains how to prepare a useful size and quantity brief.

  • Original pickup: full local date, agreed time, address and travelers boarding there.
  • Additional pickup: exact address, entrance or meeting point, joining passenger and reachable contact.
  • Combined load: total passengers, bags and other items after everyone has joined.
  • Destination: final address and any check-in, flight or event deadline the route must accommodate.

Ask the provider to check the proposed order. Two locations that look close on a map may involve different entrances, street access or a detour. Avoid promising the joining traveler a pickup time until the provider has acknowledged the plan.

Make the second pickup ready

The joining passenger should know the agreed meeting point, what to do when contacted and who manages changes. Ask them to collect stored luggage, finish checkout and complete any other departure tasks before the confirmed pickup arrangement requires them to be ready.

A hotel lobby, luggage desk and street entrance may be different places. If bag retrieval is still needed, disclose it instead of describing the stop as a simple curbside pickup. The hotel checkout and luggage guide covers that handoff.

Confirm an appropriate loading location with the provider and follow local signs. For example, SFMTA's San Francisco passenger-loading guidance describes white zones as active loading space, with operating days and hours posted. Such a zone is not a place to hold a car indefinitely while a passenger finishes packing.

Check the whole service window

Ask whether the extra stop changes the agreed pickup time, route, service end, vehicle arrangement or price. A direct transfer quote does not establish that another address is included. An hourly arrangement also needs confirmation that the revised itinerary fits its agreed window and terms.

Illustrative example: two colleagues have arranged an office-to-airport ride. A third wants to join from a hotel with a suitcase. Send the hotel location and luggage details to the provider, then ask it to review the order of stops against the airport deadline. The three travelers should receive one acknowledged plan, rather than independently telling the chauffeur which stop to visit next.

If different people also leave at different destinations, include those drop-offs in the same review. Our multiple-drop-off guide addresses that separate part of the route.

Agree on a delay fallback

Choose one organizer to communicate with the provider. Before the trip, agree what happens if the joining passenger is not ready: who calls, who can approve a change and how the rest of the group will be informed. Do not assume unlimited waiting or that the car can automatically skip a booked stop.

When timing is tight, ask the provider to compare the shared itinerary with separately arranged transportation. That is a planning option to confirm, not evidence that a second car is available. If the provider cannot acknowledge the change, the original confirmed itinerary remains the reference; do not tell the extra passenger that a new pickup has been accepted.

Send one revised ride brief

Additional pickup request
Ride reference: [reference]. Original pickup: [full local date, time and address]. Please review an additional pickup at [address and entrance] for [passenger/contact], carrying [luggage/items]. Total after this stop: [passengers and belongings]. Destination and deadline: [details]. Please confirm the stop order, pickup/readiness instructions, vehicle suitability, any revised quote or terms and the delay fallback. Organizer: [contact]. We will share the plan once you acknowledge it.

For an existing Koast reservation, use the confirmation or agreed day-of-trip contact and obtain acknowledgment before relying on an added stop. A new quote does not amend the existing ride. For a new journey, explore Koast corporate transportation or airport transfers and include every pickup in the request.
